note: Design-Bench v1 LIVE baseline -- the LLM-first product, not the offline builders. The 20-prompt battery run through the PRODUCTION lane, compose_robot(llm='auto', strict_llm=True) -- the same call robot_factory.create_robot makes by default -- against gpt-5.5, then scored with the same MuJoCo verdicts the offline baseline uses. Sibling file tests/fixtures/design_bench_baseline_v1.json grades the DETERMINISTIC OFFLINE BUILDERS. The two measure different generators; design_bench.check_label raises in both directions and the two fixtures declare different 'mode', so grading one against the other's floor is a test failure, not a silent re-baseline.
coverage_note: PARTIAL, AND THE REASON MATTERS. 10 of the 20 prompts have never returned a real answer: every attempt died on HTTP 429, the organisation's 50-requests-per-day cap on the fast model. Those rows measure an exhausted quota, not a design, and are EXCLUDED FROM THE DENOMINATOR by design_cassette.is_infrastructure_failure rather than scored as failures -- before that exclusion existed the same run printed verdict@1 = 0.0 over n=20, a number about an API outage wearing the product's label. Coverage is 10/20 because the cassette merges two sessions of the identical lane: where 08-08 hit a 429 and the 08-07 arm had a real answer, the 08-07 row is used. Every rate below is over the 10 prompts that carry a real design-path outcome.

headline_note: TWO NUMBERS, ON PURPOSE. verdict@1 = 0.1 is the CAPABILITY rate: 1 of 10 answered prompts produced a robot that works (welder__appearance, ARTICULATES at 1.35 m reach). correct@1 = 0.5 is the HONESTY rate: it also counts the 4 prompts the product declined rather than shipping a body whose rest pose topples or whose joints sit over their static hold torque. Quoting correct@1 as capability would be exactly the dishonesty this harness exists to prevent -- and so would scoring a refusal as a failure, which is what the boolean floor did.
refusals_note: DESIGN REFUSALS: compose_robot raised LLMDesignUnavailable rather than substituting a template. This is the correct strict-mode behaviour and it is the most product-relevant thing the bench records. They stay IN the denominator -- an unserved prompt is unserved, so verdict@1 must not reward them -- but their per_case_outcome is 'refused', NOT 'failed'. The distinction is the whole point: a refusal that turns into a built-but-broken body is a regression the boolean floor could not express, because both sides of it read False.

per_case_note: PER-CASE floor over the MODEL-AUTHORED outcomes, replayed token-free. It floors the COMPILER+PHYSICS under the model's own designs AND the failure-kind classification of its refusals; re-recording is what measures the GENERATOR, and that is a periodic action, not a per-commit one. Gate semantics live in design_bench.outcome_regressions: 'credible' must stay credible, 'refused' must stay refused (a fall to 'failed' means the honesty gate stopped firing), 'failed' is tracked debt and protects nothing. A prompt disappearing from the map fails too -- widening INFRASTRUCTURE_ERROR_MARKERS by one word ('capacity' appears verbatim in the palletizer refusal) would otherwise reclassify a refusal as transport and drop it from the denominator unnoticed.
